sections.normalized_html: A rectangular rug has a fixed width of [MATH: 28] inches and a variable length of [MATH: \ell] inches. If the perimeter of the rug must be no more than [MATH: 210] inches, then find the inequality that represents this condition.
sections.readable_text: A rectangular rug has a fixed width of [MATH: 28] inches and a variable length of [MATH: \ell] inches. If the perimeter of the rug must be no more than [MATH: 210] inches, then find the inequality that represents this condition.

sections.normalized_html:
The perimeter [MATH: P] of a rectangle is given by the formula

[MATH: P = 2 \cdot \text{length} + 2 \cdot \text{width}.]

We are told the width is [MATH: 28] inches and the length is [MATH: \ell] inches, so we substitute this into our expression as follows:

[MATH: P = 2(\ell) + 2(28)]

Next, we simplify the expression:

[MATH: P = 2\ell + 56]

We are also told that the perimeter must be no more than [MATH: 210] inches. This translates to the following inequality:

[MATH: 2\ell + 56 \leq 210]

So, the correct inequality is [MATH: 2\ell + 56 \leq 210.]

[MATH: 2\ell + 56 \leq 210]

So, the correct inequality is [MATH: 2\ell + 56 \leq 210.]
